title: Client Momentum Map — Deck Templates (Standard + Enterprise)
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, repeatable QBR deck family focused on two renewal motion paths: Standard (self-serve / usage-based customers) and Enterprise (committed/dedicated/private deployments). The goal: make slide assembly fast, ensure consistent renewal narratives, and provide a single source of talking points that map product telemetry to commercial outcomes.

How to use this doc:
- Choose the path: STANDARD or ENTERPRISE. Many customers will use a hybrid flow (start standard then convert to enterprise); call that out on the summary slide.
- Replace placeholders ({{CUSTOMER_NAME}}, {{OWNER}}, {{ARR}}) before sharing.
- Use the appendix for raw charts and the one-page renewal options (pricing/commit/terms).

Slide-by-slide outline (suggested order):
1) Title / Meeting Frame (1 slide)
   - Customer logo, meeting date, Redwood owner, CS exec.
   - Single-line objective: e.g., "Review usage, value delivered, and renewal options for FY26 Q3."
   - Talking note: keep execs focused on outcomes (ARR impact / risk).

2) Partnership Snapshot (1 slide)
   - Quick bullets: start date, product areas in use (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private), primary contacts, renewal date.
   - Visual: small timeline with major milestones (pilot, go-live, major feature launches).

3) Adoption & Consumption (2 slides)
   - Metrics: monthly tokens, active routes, top 3 endpoints by volume, seats/projects, average latency (p50/p95), error rates.
   - Trend charts: 6-month consumption sparkline.
   - Talking note: highlight new growth vectors (embedding adoption, multiregion requests).

4) Reliability & Quality (1 slide)
   - Uptime, incidents count (last 90d), avg incident MTTR, fallback events (model variant fallbacks), SLA adherence.
   - Annotation: call out any mitigation work (canary rollouts, redundancy).

5) Cost & Efficiency (1 slide)
   - Billing trends, cost per 1k tokens, cost-savings suggestions (batching, cache, quantization).
   - For enterprise: current Dedicated utilization vs reserved capacity.

6) Value Stories (1-2 slides)
   - Short case bullets: specific features that drove outcomes (e.g., reduced latency → 20% higher throughput for chat product).
   - Customer quotes / product metrics mapped to business KPIs.

7) Risk & Health Score (1 slide)
   - Simple colored scorecard: Usage growth, Reliability, Cost predictability, Strategic alignment.
   - Risk drivers: technical debt (old SDK), capacity constraints, security/compliance checkpoints.

8) Renewal Paths & Recommendation (1–2 slides)
   - STANDARD path (suggested for: low predictability, pay-as-you-go): forecasted ARR, recommended term, incentives (credits, feature bundles).
   - ENTERPRISE path (suggested for: predictable throughput, SLA/legal needs): committed capacity tiers, dedicated GPU pools, private deployment option with KMS/HSM integration, migration timeline.
   - Decision template: recommended path + fallback if approval delayed.

9) Commercial Options Snapshot (1 slide)
   - Clear table: Option name / Term / Committed tokens / Avg unit price / Key deliverables (SLA, support hours, onboarding).

10) Implementation & Success Plan (1 slide)
   - Owner, milestone dates, technical pre-reqs (network, KMS), enablement tasks (workshops, runbooks).

11) Ask & Next Steps (1 slide)
   - Specific asks (sign term sheet, schedule technical kickoff, approve PO), single owner per ask, target dates.

12) Appendix (variable)
   - Raw charts (weekly token graphs, route heatmap), audit log excerpts, audit/compliance summary, product release notes relevant to customer.

Renewal tracker (copy into a sheet during prep) — single-row example to paste into slide appendix:
- CUSTOMER: {{CUSTOMER_NAME}} | RENEWAL DATE: {{YYYY-MM-DD}} | CURRENT ARR: {{ARR}} | USAGE TREND: up/down/stable | RISK SCORE: low/med/high | PRIMARY RECOMMENDATION: Standard/Enterprise | OWNER: {{CS_LEAD}} | NEXT ACTION: e.g., "Send commercial proposal" | DUE: {{YYYY-MM-DD}}

Standard vs Enterprise talking points (short):
- Standard: emphasize flexibility, low friction, usage growth, self-serve billing. Offer short-term incentives (credits, pilot extension) to smooth renewal.
- Enterprise: emphasize predictability, cost optimization via reserved units, operational controls (VPC/private control plane), stronger SLAs and audit capabilities. Call out migration lift and proposed timeline (6–12 weeks typical for Dedicated migration).

Design and accessibility notes:
- Keep slides clean — 3 key messages per slide max.
- Use color coding for risk (green/amber/red).
- Include an "ask" chip top-right on slides where a decision is required.

Checklist before sending final deck:
- Replace all {{placeholders}}.
- Add 1–2 customer-specific screenshots (dashboard, sample logs).
- Cross-check billing numbers with finance owner (CON-ops billing sheet).
- Link to technical PRs/changes if incidents are referenced (link to GH/JIRA in appendix).

Open items / TODOs (prep work):
- [ ] Pull 6-month token and latency trends (owner: Jordan).
- [ ] Confirm renewal pricing bands with finance (owner: Marta).
- [ ] Create one-pager for Enterprise migration effort (owner: Riley).

Prep templates & quick copy snippets (for meeting invite):
- Subject: QBR: {{CUSTOMER_NAME}} — Partnership review & renewal discussion (30–45m)
- Opening line: "Thanks — we’ll review usage, value delivered, and proposed renewal pathways so we can align on next steps."
- Suggested attendees: CS lead, CTO/VP Eng (customer), Redwood AM, Redwood Solutions Eng.

Notes to self / collaboration cues:
- Flag any security/compliance asks early (private deployment timelines often drive commercial decisions).
- Use the rollout checklist from product-hosted-api if recommending A/B canary for a model migration (link in linked_artifacts).
- Keep an "exec one-pager" ready (single slide) for CSM to send to customer execs pre-meeting.

Historical context:
- This doc borrows structure from older QBRs but reframes around "momentum mapping" — i.e., where the account is moving and which renewal product best locks in that trajectory.

Versioning & ownership:
- Draft owner: Aisha Patel.
- Suggested naming when saving final deck: "{{CUSTOMER_NAME}} — QBR — Momentum Map — yyyy-mm-dd.pptx"

Change log (brief):
- 2025-07-11: initial draft (Aisha).
- 2025-10-02: added Enterprise migration timeline notes (Riley).
- 2026-02-28: updated cost optimization bullet and added fallback decision template (Jordan).

End of doc.
